card: Bounds pending MuSig2 signing sessions in wallet locked memory to 2048 per descriptor, evicting the oldest session nonces first. Today, unfinished MuSig2 sessions keep secret nonces in locked memory indefinitely until signed, which can consume substantial locked memory during large or abandoned multi-input signing flows. The author notes that transactions with many MuSig2 leaves can accumulate thousands of sessions, and provides a unit test demonstrating session eviction at 4096 sessions.
evidence: Author notes that unfinished MuSig2 sessions keep secret nonces in locked memory indefinitely until a partial signature is generated, risking memory bloat from concurrent or large transactions (PR description).
Author observes that standard transactions with up to ~1700 key-path inputs can quickly accumulate sessions per MuSig2 leaf, motivating a 2048 session cap per descriptor (PR description).
problem: The wallet stores MuSig2 secret nonces in locked memory indefinitely until a session completes with a partial signature or the wallet unloads. Because each MuSig2 leaf in a PSBT input initiates a session, creating many incomplete multi-input PSBTs or concurrent signing sessions can exhaust locked memory.

risk.why: Flaws in secret nonce lifecycle management or session eviction could risk MuSig2 nonce reuse or signing state corruption, which can expose private keys and lose funds.

scope_notes: The diff and file list were not provided in the patch data.
summary: Bounds the number of unfinished MuSig2 signing sessions retained in locked memory to at most 2048 per descriptor (approximately 288 KiB). Evicts the oldest session nonces first when the capacity limit is reached, requiring dropped sessions to restart from a PSBT without the wallet's public nonce. Adds a unit test verifying session bounding under 4096 initiated sessions.
uncertainties: Diff and file list were omitted, preventing verification of nonce eviction safety and memory-locking mechanics.
